body.rationale: IPS status: ratified, as given in my instructions, so the breaches in the field table are real. I put the four candidates with no hard breaches at the top and added the strongest covariance-based method that only misses on volatility. That fits the late-cycle finding (§4.3) that covariance-structure methods deserve more weight than return-forecast methods. 1) cvar_minimization: it has no breaches, the shallowest drawdown among the compliant candidates (-18.7%), and the best backtest Sharpe of that group (0.74). Its reviewer confirmed the optimiser behaves as designed. The weakness is concentration, with 2.9 effective assets, and vol tuned to exactly 8.00%. I accept that because it is a distinct tail-focused sleeve and keeps non_traditional representation in the top five for the family-span rule. I am not voting for myself. 2) resampled_efficient_frontier: it is compliant and well diversified (effective N 13.1), and resampling dampens CMA error. Its drawdown of -24.84% is only 16bp inside the limit, so I rank it below cvar_minimization. 3) inverse_volatility: it is compliant, needs no return forecast, and has simple, checkable arithmetic. Its reviewer flagged the roughly 43% in correlated credit and sovereign sleeves, which is why it is not higher. 4) black_litterman: it is compliant with a -21.9% drawdown, but the reviewer showed that the AUM-based equilibrium prior double-counts overlapping equity funds. About 49% Treasuries and 44% equity relies on the stock-bond hedge persisting. 5) risk_parity: it brings in the risk_structured family and ERC is a covariance-driven method, but its 6.5% volatility breach and the reviewers' criticism that effective N measures capital spread, not risk spread, keep it fifth. Why first beats fifth: cvar_minimization clears every hard IPS limit and has a drawdown about 1.6 points shallower than risk_parity's -20.3%, with a higher backtest Sharpe (0.74 vs 0.57). Risk_parity breaches the volatility limit and the CIO could only use it after blending. Flag: market_cap_weight breaches the drawdown limit at -40.6%, which the CRO treats as a floor, and has a CRO risk score of 0.80, the worst in the field. Its two reviewers also showed that ETF AUM is not a market portfolio and double-counts overlapping style funds. It describes itself as a diagnostic, so the CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, since its orthogonality has value in an ensemble even though it breaches return, volatility and tracking error.
